description.when: Use when a supplied exemption statute enumerates specific asset categories and imposes monetary caps or related limitations.
description.repair: Evaluate each asset independently and return every required asset key. Match the asset to the ordinary meaning and all express ownership, use, and category conditions of an operative exemption without extending one listed category to a distinct category. Under Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1123, qualifying household goods and consumer electronic devices may be covered, but jewelry is not household goods merely because it is personally owned or used. Analyze category eligibility separately from the protected amount unless the statute expressly makes value an eligibility prerequisite; under Ariz. Rev. Stat. § 33-1125(8), equity above the motor-vehicle cap limits the protected amount rather than eliminating category eligibility. Use an empty array only when no supplied operative exemption fits.
description.avoid_when: Do not apply an exemption when an express ownership, use, category, value-as-eligibility, aggregation, or other statutory condition is unsatisfied. Do not cite marital-status, proceeds, aggregation, cap, or nearby limitation provisions unless they independently protect the asset under the required citation rule.

description.when: Use when the supplied task treats category-specific exemptions together with wildcard exemptions and includes 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) or Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p).
description.repair: Apply a mandatory per-asset wildcard pass after identifying category-specific exemptions. Add 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5) to every asset for which the supplied federal exemption system is available; it may protect an interest in any property up to $1,475 plus up to $13,950 of unused § 522(d)(1) capacity. Add Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p) to every item of personal property when the supplied Oregon system is available; it may protect up to $400. Include each wildcard whenever it could protect any portion of the interest, even when a specific exemption also applies or the wildcard cannot cover the asset's full value. Do not infer exhaustion, an unavailable election, or incompatibility between supplied systems from silence. Before submission, audit every asset against each supplied wildcard and require an affirmative, fact-supported statutory reason for every omission.
description.avoid_when: Omit a wildcard only when supplied facts establish that its exemption system is unavailable, the property lies outside its express statutory scope, or its available allowance has been fully consumed. There are no additional justified exclusions.

description.when: Use this repair only when its stated factual and legal conditions apply.
description.repair: When: Use this procedure when Illinois personal-property exemptions include both the general equity exemption in 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) and category-specific provisions. Repair: Evaluate every owned, personal-use asset independently against every operative provision. Test § 12-1001(b) for any other property, subject to its $4,000 equity limit, even when a category-specific exemption also applies; a specific exemption does not displace an independently applicable general exemption. Then add each specific provision whose ordinary statutory category and factual conditions are satisfied. Treat actual garments as wearing apparel and require evidence of professional prescription for a prescribed-health-aid classification. Audit the final arrays for all overlapping exemptions. Avoid when: Do not stretch wearing apparel to jewelry or other personal adornment, and do not apply a provision when ownership, personal-use, category, prescription, or an established monetary limitation is unsatisfied.
description.avoid_when: Do not apply outside the repair's stated conditions or exceptions.

description.when: Use this repair only when its stated factual and legal conditions apply.
description.repair: When: Use this procedure when the operative exemption systems include 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5), Or. Rev. Stat. § 18.345(1)(p), or another independently applicable wildcard alongside category-specific exemptions. Repair: Evaluate category-specific provisions first, then conduct a separate mandatory wildcard pass for every asset. Add § 522(d)(5) whenever the federal system is available because it may protect an interest in any property up to $1,475 plus as much as $13,950 of unused § 522(d)(1) capacity. Add § 18.345(1)(p) whenever the Oregon system is available and the asset is personal property because it may protect up to $400. Include a wildcard even if a specific exemption also applies or the wildcard protects only part of the value. Before submitting, audit every asset against every operative wildcard and require an affirmative statutory or factual basis for each omission. Avoid when: Omit a wildcard only when the supplied facts establish that its exemption system is unavailable, the asset falls outside its express scope, or its allowance has been exhausted; never infer those conditions from silence.
description.avoid_when: Do not apply outside the repair's stated conditions or exceptions.

description.when: Use this repair only when its stated factual and legal conditions apply.
description.repair: When Illinois personal-property law supplies both 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001(b) and category-specific exemptions, use a mandatory two-pass analysis. Pass 1: identify every category-specific provision satisfied by each owned, personal-use asset. Pass 2: independently test every asset under § 12-1001(b) and include it whenever the provision may protect any equity, subject to its $4,000 limit; never omit it merely because a specific exemption also applies. Treat monetary caps as limits on the protected amount unless the statute expressly makes value an eligibility condition. Before submitting, inspect every asset array and confirm that § 12-1001(b) was either included or excluded for an express factual or statutory reason. Do not list headings, opt-out rules, or limitation provisions that do not independently exempt the asset.
description.avoid_when: Do not apply outside the repair's stated conditions or exceptions.

description.when: Use for asset-exemption mapping when every independently applicable exemption alternative must be reported, including Illinois personal-property exemptions under 735 Ill. Comp. Stat. 5/12-1001.
description.repair: For each asset, test each exemption independently against the statute’s literal category and every required fact. Treat any generally applicable exemption as a mandatory separate pass, so a specific exemption never displaces it. Under Illinois § 12-1001, first test subsection (b) for every asset: when the debtor owns the personal property and uses it personally rather than for business, include subsection (b) up to the lesser of qualifying equity, asset value, and $4,000. Then separately test subsections (a), (c), (d), and (e), retaining every supported alternative. Treat wearing apparel as clothing, require established trade use for tools, and require professional prescription for health aids. Omit unsupported alternatives rather than assigning zero; return an empty array only when no exemption applies. Before submission, audit every asset—including assets already assigned a specific exemption—for any omitted general exemption, while preserving all required asset keys and permitted schema fields.
description.avoid_when: Do not infer eligibility from an available citation label, a merely possible use, or an unsupported classification. Do not treat adornment as apparel, use zero-value placeholders for category mismatches, or stop after finding one exemption. Apply Illinois-specific categories and limits only to Illinois § 12-1001; there are no additional exclusions justified by the supplied evidence.

description.when: Use this repair only when its stated factual and legal conditions apply.
description.repair:
When: The task requests every independently applicable exemption and federal exemptions are permitted.
Repair: Evaluate every asset through a mandatory three-part checklist: specific federal categories, 11 U.S.C. § 522(d)(5), and applicable state categories. Never stop after finding a specific exemption. Section 522(d)(5) can apply to any property and may coexist with a category-specific exemption; its ceiling is $1,475 plus up to $13,950 of unused § 522(d)(1) capacity. For each alternative, independently set claim_value to the lesser of the debtor’s interest, the asset value, and the available statutory limit. Before returning JSON, audit every asset row and record either a § 522(d)(5) claim or a concrete statutory or factual reason for excluding it. Use every required asset key and exact permitted citation labels.
Avoid when: Do not use § 522(d)(5) when federal exemptions are unavailable, the debtor has no interest in the property, or the supplied facts show no remaining wildcard capacity. A citation’s presence alone does not establish eligibility.
description.avoid_when: Do not apply outside the repair's stated conditions or exceptions.
